newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian money rates ease, trade picks up.
newsitem.headline: Croatian money rates ease, trade picks up.

text.p: Croatian money market rates eased somewhat in livelier trade on Thursday, as high bank liquidity continued, dealers said.
"The extremely high liquidity is continuing and all banks are positive so there was no overnight trade on Wednesday," one dealer told Reuters.
But daily trade on the Croatian money market had picked up after a lull earlier in the week, she said.
Fresh deals struck by 0830 GMT amounted to 19.3 million kuna, compared to seven million the previous day. The offer of kuna funds was strong, leaving a surplus of 150 million on the supply side.
Most borrowers sought only term loans, so call money deals, usually making up a large portion of transactions, amounted only to 500,000 kuna, granted at a lower rate of seven percent.
One-month loans were granted at 12 and 13 percent, down from Wednesday's weighted rate of 15.2 percent.
Two- and three-month loans were struck at 18 percent.

Banks had 21.3 million kuna in outstanding Lombard loans, down from Wednesday's 25.2 million, while banks' accounts fell to 620 million kuna from 657 million the previous day. -- Zoran Radosavljevic, Zagreb Newsroom +385 1 455 7075
